subject: Pricing variance request for AWS listing - EdgeGrid Logistics
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah@edgegrid.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Amit Desai <amit.desai@edgegrid.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: AWS marketplace listing - pricing flexibility request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency and the model routing controls. Procurement has been reviewing the AWS Marketplace private offer, and they've pushed back on the list price for our use case. We need an additional one-time concession on the listing price (effectively a 20% reduction on the first-year committed spend) in order to go live via marketplace — otherwise procurement will insist on a direct contract, which slows our timeline.

Details:
- Expected first-year committed spend: $240,000
- Desired marketplace-effective price reduction: ~20% on the public offer to align with procurement targets
- Timeline: need a final offer by Apr 20 to make the Q2 ingest window

I attached the high-level SOW and estimated AWS procurement worksheet. Can Redwood support a pricing variance or special listing rate if we commit to a 12-month term and co-sell motion?

Appreciate any options you can share.

Best,
Hannah Li
Head of Cloud Procurement
EdgeGrid Logistics
Attachment: EdgeGrid_AWS_PO_SOW.pdf (PDF stub)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Li <hannah@edgegrid.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS marketplace listing - pricing flexibility request

Hi Hannah — thanks for the note and for sending the SOW. This is doable in principle but I'll need to run a short internal approval through Deal Desk and get Marketplace listing guidance from Jonas.

Ben / Jonas / Sergio — looping you in. EdgeGrid is asking for ~20% effective reduction on the first-year spend if they commit to 12 months and a co-sell banner + joint announcement. Attached is their SOW and TCV model Hannah sent.

Quick asks to help our evaluation:
- Confirm whether the suggested concession can be packaged as a marketplace private offer (AWS PO) vs a manual credit. AWS wants a clean private-offer flow.
- If we approve a listing variance, what are guardrails on minimum TCV, required co-sell commitments, and marketing deliverables?
- Any immediate SLA/operational constraints we should call out (e.g., dedicated capacity requests)?

Hannah — we'll come back with an internal recommendation within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: EdgeGrid_TCV_Model.xlsx (XLSX stub)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: AWS marketplace listing - pricing flexibility request

Marissa / team — thanks for the context. A few points from Deal Desk perspective before we escalate to an approval path: 

1) Business case: need a one-page justification (I drafted bullets below you can edit) showing ARR/TCV, margin impact at list price vs proposed concession, and high-level references to comps (we usually allow a one-off marketplace reduction for strategic co-sell customers but need to see that it still meets minimum unit economics).

2) Guardrails proposed (suggested):
- Minimum 12-month commitment with a $200k net committed ARR floor after concession
- Public listing remains at standard list price; marketplace private-offer will carry the concession (so we record list price for metrics)
- Co-sell requirements: joint case study + webinar within Q3 and inclusion in our marketplace featured slot for 90 days
- Limited one-time marketing credit in lieu of additional discount if they agree to co-marketing deliverables

3) Approvals: We can approve up to 15% effective concession under standard delegated authority with product/ops sign-off. Anything >15% requires VP Revenue approval and a business justification signed by the AE and the CRO.

Items I need to route for VP approval (if we go >15%):
- Final TCV model (row-level) — please attach the detailed sheets
- Procurement language they will push into AWS PO (we need to validate revenue recognition and billing flow)
- A statement of expected strategic value (co-sell lift, logos, reference value)

Marissa — can you confirm whether EdgeGrid will accept the co-sell/marketing commitments? If yes, attach the detailed TCV model and I’ll run numbers.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations (Deal Desk)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: marketplace-offer-draft.json (JSON stub)

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Li <hannah@edgegrid.com>, Amit Desai <amit.desai@edgegrid.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS marketplace listing - pricing flexibility request

Hi all — thanks for the patience. I reviewed Ben’s model and our Ops constraints. Decision & conditions below: 

Approval summary:
- Approved: 18% effective concession off first-year public list when implemented as an AWS Marketplace private offer (EdgeGrid receives private-offer price)
- Required commitments from EdgeGrid: 12-month commitment, minimum net first-year spend $200k after concession, co-sell banner + joint webinar within 90 days of go-live, and permission to use EdgeGrid as a reference customer in our marketplace materials.
- Marketing credit: $15k co-marketing credit (applied as a separate invoice credit) in lieu of deeper price cut if they meet all deliverables within 120 days.

Operational notes:
- Marketplace flow: We will publish the private-offer SKU with the concession and validate billing flow with AWS. Please ensure procurement's AWS PO references the private-offer ID (do not create a parallel direct contract).
- Capacity: EdgeGrid's projected peak can be handled on our Dedicated pool under standard autoscale; no dedicated pod needed initially. If they exceed 90th percentile monthly throughput, we will revisit.

Next steps (owner):
- Marissa: Confirm EdgeGrid accepts the commitment package and send signed PO by Apr 20.
- Ben: I need the final TCV spreadsheet (detailed rows) to record margin impact and for VP archive.
- Marissa/EdgeGrid: I’ll prepare the private-offer draft and DocuSign link for the PO.

Hannah / Amit — please confirm within 24 hours if you accept these conditions and we’ll push the private-offer through AWS.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Marketplace Partnerships Lead
Redwood Inference
